original_concern.concern: Proof 3.1 says the complement-cover identification extends smoothly because it preserves boundary monodromies. Monodromy alone supplies no smooth extension across a square branch chart: for example, a nonconformal real-linear normal germ generally has no differentiable square-root lift. The argument needs an explicit tubular normalization or compatible transported branch charts, including the claimed independence from arbitrary tubular charts in 2.1. The isotopy-invariance conclusion is standard, but this smoothness step is not justified as written.

original_cases.reason: Equality of monodromies classifies covers only away from the branch core. For example A(x+iy)=2x+iy is orientation preserving but not complex conformal. A differentiable lift h of A(z²) under squaring would have a real-linear invertible derivative B with (Bz)²=A(z²); writing Bz=az+b conjugate(z), the missing |z|² coefficient forces ab=0, and orientation then forces b=0, inconsistent with the conjugate(z)² coefficient of A(z²). Thus the current claimed extension is unjustified. The proposal normalizes tubes to a rotation by equal-normal-derivative tubular uniqueness and a positive-definite polar homotopy, then supplies an actual smooth square-root phase. For isotopy invariance it first transports charts. The Statement remains the same oriented total-space diffeomorphism assertion; no stronger smooth isomorphism over a fixed identity base map is asserted.

proposals.source_excerpt: 2.1 By [F3] and [F4], the index-two kernel determines a connected two-sheeted cover. On the boundary of a punctured tube around $K_i$, its two monodromies are the prescribed meridian value $1$ and a longitude value $\eta_i\in\mathbb F_2$. The local model [F5] has exactly those two monodromies; classification of covers of the punctured tube identifies it with the restricted cover. The displayed model therefore extends the cover across every branch component. If a tubular framing is changed by $k$ meridional twists, the parallel longitude changes by $k\mu_i$, so its character changes by $k$ modulo two; the corresponding rotation of the normal coordinate changes the phase in the local model by the same parity. Thus these are coordinate descriptions of one extension, not different covers. [F3, F4, F5, step 1.1]
proposals.proposed_replacement:
2.1 By [F3] and [F4], the index-two kernel determines a connected two-sheeted cover. On a punctured tube around $K_i$, its two monodromies are the meridian value $1$ and a longitude value $\eta_i\in\mathbb F_2$. The local model [F5] has exactly these monodromies, so covering classification identifies its punctured part with the restricted cover. Attach its core to obtain a smooth extension in the chosen charts. This constructs an extension; independence of the smooth total-space diffeomorphism type requires the normalization below, not merely equality of boundary monodromies. [F3, F4, F5, step 1.1]

2.2 Compare two oriented tubular charts $\varphi_0,\varphi_1$ around the same component. Express them over a common oriented core parameter $s$; a change of the original core parameter only replaces the unit phase $e^{\mathrm i\eta_j s}$ by a smooth unit loop $a_j(s)$ of the same winding number $\eta_j$. Let $A(s)\in GL^+(2,\mathbb R)$ be the unique vertical linear change for which $\varphi_1\circ A$ and $\varphi_0$ induce the same normal-quotient identification. Write $A=RP$ by smooth polar decomposition, with $R(s)\in SO(2)$ and $P(s)$ positive definite. The compatible-tube assertion [F6] gives an ambient isotopy fixing the core and carrying $\varphi_0$ to $\varphi_1\circ A$ near it. The fiber-linear isotopy $R((1-t)P+tI)$ then connects $A$ to $R$ through invertible maps. On a common smaller tube its composition with $\varphi_1$ is an isotopy of open embeddings, with open track, fixing the core. The relative open-set clause of [F6] extends it near the compact core. Thus an ambient diffeomorphism $g$, isotopic to the identity through maps fixing the whole link, satisfies $g\circ\varphi_0=\varphi_1\circ R$ near this component. Choose the supports in disjoint component tubes and compose the finitely many isotopies. [F6, given, construct]

2.3 Identify $R(s)$ with a unit complex number, of winding $k$. The image under $g$ of the first chart longitude has slope $\lambda_1+k\mu$ in the second chart, so preservation of the meridian character gives $\eta_0\equiv\eta_1+k\pmod2$. The unit loop $R(s)a_0(s)/a_1(s)$ therefore has even winding. It has a smooth periodic square root $r(s)$: lift its argument on $[0,2\pi]$, halve it, and use even winding to match the endpoints and derivatives. In the two branch models $b_j(s,z)=(s,a_j(s)z^2)$ the map $(s,z)\mapsto(s,r(s)z)$ consequently covers $g$, since $a_1r^2=Ra_0$. It is an orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphism including $z=0$. The two signs of $r$ differ by the deck map. Choose the sign matching the complement-cover isomorphism at one point of each connected punctured tube; covering uniqueness makes them agree throughout that tube. Hence the local lifts glue to the complement lift. This proves independence of the oriented smooth total-space diffeomorphism type from arbitrary oriented tubular charts. It does not assert a smooth lift over the identity base map between arbitrary unnormalized charts. [F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

proposals.source_excerpt: 3.1 The based covering uniqueness in [F4] identifies the two complement covers over this diffeomorphism. The identification extends over each branch tube because it preserves the two boundary monodromies in step 2.1; the local order-two models then give an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed branched covers. Thus $\Sigma(L')\cong\Sigma(L)$ as oriented manifolds. [F4, F5, step 2.1, step 1.2] ∎
proposals.proposed_replacement: 3.1 Let $F$ be the terminal diffeomorphism of the given ambient isotopy from $L$ to $L'$. First choose the target tubular charts by transporting the source charts through $F$. Corresponding longitudes have the same character, and in these transported branch coordinates a lift is $(s,z)\mapsto(s,z)$, or its deck translate. By step 1.2 and [F4] the complement covers are isomorphic over $F$; on every punctured tube that isomorphism is one of these two local lifts, so it extends smoothly across the branch core. The resulting map is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed total spaces. Finally steps 2.2–2.3 compare the transported target charts with any originally chosen target charts. Thus $\Sigma(L')\cong\Sigma(L)$ as oriented manifolds, with no unjustified smooth extension of an arbitrary normal germ. [F4, F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3] ∎

proposals.source_excerpt: [F5] The local normal-disk model for a branch component is $(s,z)\mapsto(s,e^{\mathrm i\eta s}z^2)$ with $s\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$; its meridian monodromy is nontrivial and its longitudinal monodromy is $\eta\in\mathbb F_2$ ([[def-double-branched-cover-of-an-oriented-link]]).
proposals.proposed_replacement:
[F5] The local normal-disk model for a branch component is $(s,z)\mapsto(s,e^{\mathrm i\eta s}z^2)$ with $s\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$; its meridian monodromy is nontrivial and its longitudinal monodromy is $\eta\in\mathbb F_2$ ([[def-double-branched-cover-of-an-oriented-link]]).

[F6] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, two tubular embeddings of the same normal bundle inducing the same vertical normal-quotient map are ambient isotopic near a compact core, fixing that core ([[cor-tubular-neighbourhoods-are-unique-up-to-ambient-isotopy]]). The relative open-set clause of [[thm-isotopy-extension]] also extends an isotopy of an ambient open set with open track near any compact subset. In the application the ambient manifold is the boundaryless $S^3$, the core is the compact union of link circles, the normal identifications are explicitly equalized, and the fiber-linear isotopy consists of open embeddings after a common shrinking. AC implies the required countable choice.

Its double branched cover is $\#^{\,k-1}(S^2\times S^1)$, with $\Sigma(U_1)=S^3$. Over $\mathbb F_2$, the hat Floer group of this cover is identified with the exterior algebra on a $(k-1)$-dimensional vector space, hence has rank $2^{k-1}$. Under these identifications, the cobordism maps for saddle cobordisms between neighboring unlink resolutions, with $p$ carried outside the saddle disk, are the multiplication and comultiplication maps of the two-dimensional Frobenius algebra $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$ after reduction at the marked component. The identification includes the marked-circle cases and fixes the basis conventions needed to compare the first surgery differential with the reduced Khovanov cube.

proposals.source_excerpt: Its abelianization under $x\mapsto q$, $y\mapsto p$ is $cq-dp=-1$, so it is opposite the positive normal-disk meridian, whose class is the positive generator by [F3].
proposals.proposed_replacement: To calibrate signs geometrically, the positively oriented coordinate cores representing $x$ and $y$ bound the hemispherical disks $D_x=\{\operatorname{Im}z_2=0,\ \operatorname{Re}z_2\ge0\}\cap S^3$ and $D_y=\{\operatorname{Im}z_1=0,\ \operatorname{Re}z_1\ge0\}\cap S^3$, oriented by their respective core boundaries. The knot meets $D_x$ transversely in $|q|$ points, each with intersection sign $\operatorname{sgn}(q)$, and meets $D_y$ in $|p|$ points, each with sign $\operatorname{sgn}(p)$. For the first sign, at a point where $z_2$ is positive real, the ambient orientation is the complex $z_1$ orientation followed by increasing $\operatorname{Im}z_2$; the component of the knot tangent transverse to $D_x$ has sign $q$. For the second, at positive real $z_1$, the ambient orientation is increasing $\operatorname{Im}z_1$ followed by the complex $z_2$ orientation, and the transverse tangent component has sign $p$. Deleting small disks about these intersections gives oriented surfaces in the knot complement with boundary relations $[x]=q[\mu]$ and $[y]=p[\mu]$, where $\mu$ is the positive normal-disk meridian. Thus the abelianization $x\mapsto q$, $y\mapsto p$ sends this geometric meridian to $1$: [F3] makes $[\mu]$ a generator, and the displayed relations and $\gcd(p,q)=1$ fix its sign. The disk-boundary curve $m$ has abelianization $cq-dp=-1$, so its orientation is opposite to that positive meridian.

proposals.source_excerpt:
$g_i^{\pm1}T_\mu$. In each current diagram, orient open strands from the smaller to the larger endpoint
   label and order them by their initial endpoints. Order closed components by
   their least segment labels. In each closed component, start by traversing its
   least-labelled segment from its designated initial endpoint to its terminal
   endpoint; then follow the unique continuation of that component, traversing
   later segments in whichever direction reaches the next endpoint. At a crossing
   continue along the same strand, and after a smoothing continue along the
   prescribed pairing. Retain segment labels and their designated endpoints
   through switches and smoothings. This gives a deterministic traversal even
   when segment orientations do not join coherently around a closed component.
proposals.proposed_replacement:
$g_i^{\pm1}T_\mu$. For each initial reducer input (a matrix column here or a
   closed trace diagram in Step 5), first fix pairwise disjoint rational crossing
   boxes, each meeting only its two crossing branches, in four boundary ports,
   and containing no polygonal vertex. Choose the first admissible finite tuple
   in the length-then-lexicographic rational coding order of Step 3. Make the
   boxes small enough that every component contains a segment portion outside
   the boxes. Subdivide all polygonal segments at their box-boundary ports.
   Give the portions outside the boxes fresh distinct labels in their finite
   diagram-code order; designate the lexicographically smaller coordinate
   endpoint of each portion as its initial endpoint. Retain these portions,
   labels, and endpoints throughout that reduction tree. Inside each box record
   either the original crossing pairing or one of its two smoothing pairings;
   switches change only over/under data, and smoothings change only this pairing.
   In each current diagram, orient open strands from the smaller to the larger
   boundary endpoint label and order them by their initial endpoints. Order
   closed components by their least portion labels. Start each closed component
   along its least-labelled portion from its designated initial endpoint to its
   other endpoint, then follow its unique continuation. Inside a crossing box
   follow its current pairing. No portion is split or relabelled by a switch or
   smoothing, and every resulting component contains a labelled portion. This
   determines the traversal even when the designated directions of successive
   portions disagree.

original_concern.concern: Proof 1.2 says the classes are rationally independent because 'a rational relation clears denominators to the excluded nonzero signed integer relation.' Clearing denominators initially gives an integer combination that is torsion modulo the filtration, rather than necessarily zero there. original_cases.reason: The proof first excludes every nonzero integer coefficient vector modulo F_{n+1}^{top}, with coefficients unbounded in magnitude. This is an injection Z^{m+1} into the abelian quotient. Rational localization preserves that injection: a rational relation yields, after clearing coefficient denominators, a torsion integer combination; multiplying by its finite order gives a nonzero integer coefficient vector in F_{n+1}^{top}, already excluded. Thus no extra obstruction hypothesis or mathematical prerequisite is missing. The sentence compresses this standard localization algebra; spelling out the torsion step, as the smooth supplier does in 2.1–3.1, would aid a reader but is optional clarification rather than an actual soundness defect.

proposals.source_excerpt: **Finite comparison rules:** Two normalized codes represent the same code class when some bijection of their finite crossing labels and edge labels carries all dart incidences, crossing rotations, orientations, signs, component cycles, and outer-face data of one code to the other. To test whether two codes differ by one move, enumerate all finite choices of local edge intervals and crossing subrecords of sizes allowed by R1, R2, or R3; test that the codes agree outside the chosen disk boundary and that the two local records are one of the standard orientation/sign variants of that move. The local-site test uses the exact variants in the oriented Reidemeister-move definition.
proposals.proposed_replacement:
**Finite comparison rules:** Two normalized codes represent the same code class when some bijection of their finite crossing labels and edge labels carries all dart incidences, crossing rotations, orientations, signs, component cycles, and outer-face data of one code to the other. For a move-site test use the finite spherical cellulation returned by reconstruction and mark a point at infinity in its distinguished outer face. For the crossingless circle, insert one auxiliary degree-two vertex and use its two complementary face disks; this vertex is suppressed in all comparisons.

For each of $m=2,4,6$, enumerate every distribution of $m$ distinct cut points among diagram edges and every linear order of the points on each edge. Use one representative of each order (for example equally spaced interior points); their numerical positions are immaterial. In each face disk enumerate noncrossing pairings of all boundary occurrences of these cut points by interior arcs. In the distinguished face also record which complementary region contains the marked point at infinity. Glue the face arcs at the cut points and retain only choices forming a single simple closed curve. Cutting the finite cellulation along these arcs and flooding across incident cell pieces identifies the two sides; select the side not containing infinity. This is the candidate closed move disk. Its entire diagram intersection, including every vertex, edge segment and possible closed component inside it, must be isomorphic relative to its cyclically ordered boundary points to one side of a standard R1, R2 or R3 template with the chosen orientation/sign variant. In particular no additional diagram portion is permitted inside the disk. All tests are finite incidence and cyclic-order comparisons. The same construction is performed for the other code, requiring the opposite side of the same template and an isomorphism of the outside records fixing the ordered boundary points, all decorations and the infinity region. Store the cut orders, face pairings, selected regions, template variant and outside isomorphism as the certificate.

There are finitely many cut distributions, orders, face pairings and region choices. Every move disk has two, four or six transverse boundary intersections, avoids crossing vertices, and cuts each face into disjoint arcs; it therefore has a representative among these choices. Moving cut points along an edge and face arcs within a face disk changes neither the inside tangle nor the outside code class. Thus the test includes every admissible move disk, including move creation from the crossingless circle, and accepts only genuine disk-supported template replacements. The local templates and their exact orientation/sign variants are those in the oriented Reidemeister-move definition.

original_concern.concern: The uniform needle bound lacks a uniform separation hypothesis. Step 1.2 says, “compactness and embeddedness give a uniform positive lower bound for |z-z′|,” but embeddedness for each ε and compact control of the critical-point charts do not prevent another regular strand from approaching the needle as ε→0. Locally take the fixed Morse cap z=s, t=−s², |s|≤ε/2, and another upward strand z=iε. The cap has horizontal diameter ε and its critical chart is unchanged. Its two signed degree-one mixed-chord integrals sum, up to orientation sign, to (2πi)⁻¹ log((1/2−i)/(−1/2−i)), a nonzero constant; the chord joins different skeleton components and survives tangle 1T. These local pieces can be extended by regular arcs inside a fixed slab. Thus the written chart assumptions do not justify Cmε uniformly. The cited CDM §8.6.2 argument also uses opposite-branch cancellation rather than the claimed individual absolute long-chord estimate. The convergence assertion for a fixed tangle is a separate issue.

proposals.source_excerpt: For every fixed $m$, the sum of degree-$m$ pairing integrals that have at least one endpoint on $N_\varepsilon$ has norm at most $C_m\varepsilon$, where $C_m$ is independent of $\varepsilon$. Thus these contributions tend to zero as the needle narrows.
proposals.proposed_replacement: For the following uniform local-cap estimate, assume additionally a fixed finite system of disjoint critical bands and intervening regular bands, with uniformly bounded branch derivatives in their height or Morse coordinates. Assume the critical charts vary in a compact smooth family and their linear terms are uniformly bounded away from zero, and that every equal-height pair other than the two branches meeting at the same critical point has horizontal separation at least a fixed $d>0$, independent of $\varepsilon$. Require $N_\varepsilon$ to lie in one of these Morse charts with parameter range $0\le s\le A\varepsilon$, for a fixed $A$. Then, for every fixed $m$, the sum of degree-$m$ pairing integrals with at least one endpoint on $N_\varepsilon$ has norm at most $C_m\varepsilon$, with $C_m$ independent of $\varepsilon$. Thus these contributions tend to zero under these uniformity hypotheses. No such uniform estimate is asserted for an unrelated strand approaching the needle as $\varepsilon\to0$; convergence for each fixed knot or tangle is unaffected.

proposals.source_excerpt: 1.2 For a long chord with one endpoint on the needle and one outside it, compactness and embeddedness give a uniform positive lower bound for $|z-z'|$ on each compact branch chart. In the Morse parameter $s$, both endpoint evaluations are smooth, so the one-form $d\log(z-z')$ has norm at most $C\,ds$. The range of $s$ along a width-$\varepsilon$ needle is at most $C\varepsilon$, since $|z_+(s)-z_-(s)|\asymp s$. Thus integrating such a chord endpoint over any subinterval of the needle costs at most $C\varepsilon$. This is a direct absolute estimate for each pairing term and does not identify diagrams obtained from opposite branch choices. The constants are uniform in the stated compact smooth family. [given, F1, F2, construct, algebra]
proposals.proposed_replacement: 1.2 For a fixed knot or tangle, a long chord in a sufficiently small critical chart has nonzero limiting separation at the critical point, so its denominator is bounded below by some positive constant. In the uniform local-cap family, the additional separation hypothesis supplies the same lower bound $d$ independently of $\varepsilon$. The branch derivative bounds in the Morse parameter give $|d(z-z')|\le C\,ds$, hence $|d\log(z-z')|\le (C/d)\,ds$ uniformly. The stipulated range $0\le s\le A\varepsilon$ then bounds the integral of this factor by $CA\varepsilon/d$; on a subinterval $(0,\delta)$ it is at most $C\delta/d$. These are individual absolute estimates under the stated uniformity hypotheses. They do not replace the opposite-branch cancellation used for more general special critical movements in the cited sources. [given, F1, F2, construct, algebra]

original_concern.concern: The Definition starts with an arbitrary balanced sutured manifold and says: 'Two such fields are homologous when, outside some open ball in int M, they are homotopic'. Balanced manifolds here may be disconnected. On two disjoint product balls, take fields v, w, z with the fixed boundary values: w differs from v by one local Hopf modification in the first component, and z differs from w by one in the second. Then v is related to w and w to z, but v is not related to z: a single ball lies in one component, leaving a nontrivial relative Hopf difference in the other. Thus the stated relation is not transitive and does not define homology classes at this scope. The empty balanced manifold also has no ball witnessing reflexivity. The original [Juhász 2006, §4](https://msp.org/agt/2006/6-3/agt-v6-n3-p16-s.pdf) explicitly assumes connectedness before this definition. The actual knot exteriors are connected, but the general definition needs adjudication.

original_cases.reason: Confirmed genuine equivalence-relation defect at the full approved balanced-manifold scope. The balanced Definition explicitly permits compact disconnected and empty M. On two disjoint standard product balls, normalize a reference nonzero field and make an interior Hopf modification in the first, then another in the second. Consecutive fields are related by deleting the appropriate one ball, but the first and last are not: deleting a connected ball leaves the nonzero relative pi_3(S²) Hopf difference in the other component. For empty M, even reflexivity fails because there is no ball witnessing the existential condition. The cached Juhasz2006§4 explicitly assumes connectedness before Definition4.2. Preserve the broad manifold scope by using the existing connected relation COMPONENTWISE, with the empty condition vacuous; do not narrow M to connected. Compact manifolds have finitely many components, so this is a finite product of equivalence relations and adds no choice assumption.

replacements.source_excerpt: 1.2 Suppose that $\lambda$ is a translation-invariant Borel measure finite on every bounded Borel set. Put $U_j=\{x:\|x-e_j\|_2<1/3\}$. For $j\ne k$, $\|e_j-e_k\|_2=\sqrt2>2/3$, so the $U_j$ are pairwise disjoint. Each lies in the bounded ball $\{x:\|x\|_2<2\}$ by the triangle inequality. Translation invariance gives $\lambda(U_j)=m$ independent of $j$. If $m>0$, the first $N$ disjoint balls have total measure $Nm$ for every $N$, contradicting finiteness of the radius-two ball. Hence $m=0$. [F2, given, algebra]
replacements.proposed_replacement: 1.2 Suppose that $\lambda$ is a nonzero locally finite translation-invariant Borel measure, where locally finite means that every point has a neighborhood of finite measure. At zero choose $R>0$ with $\lambda(B(0,R))<\infty$. Put $r=R/8$ and $U_j=B((R/2)e_j,r)$. For $j\ne k$ the distance between the centers is $R/\sqrt2>2r$, so these balls are pairwise disjoint, and every $U_j$ lies in $B(0,R)$ because $R/2+r<R$. Translation invariance gives a common finite mass $m=\lambda(U_j)$. If $m>0$, finite additivity and monotonicity give $Nm\le\lambda(B(0,R))$ for every $N$, a contradiction. Hence $m=0$. This covers in particular every measure finite on all bounded Borel sets, since that condition implies local finiteness. [F2, F4, given, algebra]

replacements.source_excerpt: 2.1 Translation invariance and step 1.2 make every radius-$1/3$ ball have measure zero. Let $D$ be the set of finitely supported rational sequences. [F3] makes $D$ countable: it is the countable union, over support lengths $N$, of the countable set $\mathbb Q^N$ padded with zeros. It is dense in $\ell^2$: for any $x\in\ell^2$ and $\epsilon>0$, choose $N$ so that the squared tail sum is less than $\epsilon^2/4$, then approximate the first $N$ coordinates by rationals with squared total error less than $\epsilon^2/4$; the resulting padded vector is within $\epsilon$ of $x$. The radius-$1/3$ balls centered at $D$ therefore form a countable cover of $\ell^2$. By [F2], $\lambda(\ell^2)=0$, and [F4] makes every Borel subset null. This contradicts that $\lambda$ is nonzero. Hence no such reference measure exists, refuting the statement; in particular, the displayed Gaussian has no density relative to one. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.2, given, algebra, choose] ∎

proposals.source_excerpt: [F4] [[def-ip-isonormal-white-noise-experiment]] and [[lem-standard-normal-fourth-moment]]: the noise coordinates are independent standard normals with even density, first and third moments zero, and second and fourth moments $1$ and $3$.
proposals.proposed_replacement: [F4] [[def-ip-isonormal-white-noise-experiment]] supplies independent standard-normal coordinates with normalized density $\varphi(t)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-t^2/2}$ and covariance one. We use the scalar calculation of [[lem-standard-normal-fourth-moment]] with this supplied law, rather than invoke its AC-based law construction: $\varphi\prime(t)=-t\varphi(t)$, so integration by parts on $[-R,R]$ gives $\int t^2\varphi=[-t\varphi]_{-R}^R+\int\varphi$ and $\int t^4\varphi=[-t^3\varphi]_{-R}^R+3\int t^2\varphi$. The polynomial-Gaussian boundary terms vanish as $R\to\infty$; the nonnegative integrals increase to their full integrals. Supplied normalization therefore gives second and fourth moments $1$ and $3$; symmetry gives first and third moments zero. This supplied-law calculation uses no additional choice.

original_concern.concern: The Statement defines a positive Hopf band solely as 'an oriented annulus whose two boundary components, with their induced orientations, have linking number +1.' This omits the unknotted-core condition. A framed annulus around a nontrivial knot can satisfy this linking condition. Knotting the b-annulus away from the plumbing square and the specified disk for a⁺ preserves the stated linking/intersection conditions and matrix calculation, but does not justify the trefoil boundary identification in Proof 1.1. The later word 'standard' needs an explicit restriction consistent with the initial definition. The conventional missing condition is explicit in Quach Hongler–Weber, §2, printed p. 137: [The link of an extrovert divide](https://www.numdam.org/article/AFST_2000_6_9_1_133_0.pdf). Thus the definition and trefoil identification appear overbroad as written, although the displayed matrix follows from the other specified conditions.

original_cases.reason: Linking of the induced annulus boundaries fixes its framing, not its knot type. A tubular annulus with nontrivial core and this framing meets the written definition. Local knotting of the second annulus away from the plumbing square and the first push-off disk does not change the given framing/intersection/linking conditions. Proof1.1, in contrast, uses the actual standard disk-and-three-band model; that geometric identification does not follow for these more general annuli. Add the missing unknotted-core condition for the conventional trefoil assertion and retain the original matrix-only result for all annuli satisfying the original hypotheses, since Proof2.1 depends only on those data.

proposals.source_excerpt: Finite basis-coordinate cylinder rectangles have the product of their marginal probabilities; since they form a generating pi-system for the joint Borel and basis-observation sigma-algebras, [F9] extends this identity and proves that $W$ is independent of $\mathcal G:=\sigma(Y(e_n):n)$. To compare with the full field sigma-algebra, write the supplied basis of $H$ as $e_1,\ldots,e_m$ if finite, allowing $m=0$, or as $(e_n)_{n\ge1}$ if countably infinite. For finite $m$ put $P_Ng=\sum_{1\le n\le\min(N,m)}\langle g,e_n\rangle_He_n$; for an infinite basis put $P_Ng=\sum_{1\le n\le N}\langle g,e_n\rangle_He_n$. In either case the empty sum is zero, $r_N:=g-P_Ng$ tends to zero, and in the finite or empty case $r_N=0$ after the basis is exhausted. The mean-square error of $D_N:=Y(g)-Y(P_Ng)$ is at most $(\|Km_0\|^2+\|K\|^2\|C_0\|+\epsilon^2)\|r_N\|^2$. Choose the least $N_k\ge k$ with $\|r_{N_k}\|\le2^{-k}$. For each positive integer $r$, Markov gives $\mathbb P(|D_{N_k}|\ge1/r)\le r^2(\|Km_0\|^2+\|K\|^2\|C_0\|+\epsilon^2)4^{-k}$, a summable bound; [F11] implies $|D_{N_k}|<1/r$ eventually almost surely. The countable intersection over $r$ still has probability one, so $D_{N_k}\to0$ and each field evaluation is measurable with respect to the completion $\overline{\mathcal G}^{\mathbb P}$. Thus $\sigma(Y(g):g\in H)\subseteq\overline{\mathcal G}^{\mathbb P}$. Independence of $W$ from $\mathcal G$ extends to its completion because every completed event differs by a null set from an event in $\mathcal G$; therefore $W$ is independent of the full field. [given, F3, F6, F7, F9, F11, F12, step 3.1, step 4.1, choose, construct, algebra]
proposals.proposed_replacement: For a fixed finite list of observations, finite basis-coordinate cylinder rectangles and observation rectangles have the product of their marginal probabilities by the independence just proved. These rectangles form a generating pi-system for the product of the residual Borel sigma-algebra and the finite observation Borel sigma-algebra, so [F9] extends the product identity and shows that $W$ is independent of this finite observation block. Now fix any $A\in\mathcal B(X)$. The finite measures $C\mapsto\mathbb P(W\in A,C)$ and $C\mapsto\mathbb P(W\in A)\mathbb P(C)$ agree on the pi-system of finite observation cylinder events, including the whole space. By [F9] they agree on $\sigma(Y(g):g\in H)$. Since this holds for every $A$, $W$ is independent of the full field. This argument includes finite and empty supplied bases and requires no inclusion in the ordinary completion of a basis-observation sigma-algebra. original_concern.concern: Proof 2.1 says the expansion of (θ⊥·∇)^m has 'all coefficients ... bounded by one'. In the collected multi-index expansion, binomial factors occur: for m = 3 and θ⊥ = (1/√2,1/√2), the mixed-derivative coefficient is 3/(2√2) > 1. Uniform bounds depending on m suffice for the claimed C_m estimate; alternatively the expansion can explicitly retain ordered derivative terms.

original_cases.reason: The objection uses the collected multi-index expansion. The text does not require that expansion: expanding the m successive factors as a sum over ordered coordinate-derivative choices yields 2^m terms, each coefficient a product of m components of theta-perp and hence bounded in magnitude by one. Their L2 norms are bounded by the finite sum of the fixed smooth bump derivative norms, uniformly in theta. Collection produces binomial factors but neither collection nor a unit bound on collected coefficients is needed. The existing C_m is allowed to depend on m. Naming ordered terms would clarify a sound proof; this is not a required repair.

The existing statement and formal-series proof correctly express dependence on proper contiguous subwords; change the display title only.

original_concern.concern: The Definition instructs one to glue x and y from two ordinary complex skein modules, sets B_Σ(x,y)=Z_p(S³,Γ,w), and then declares this conjugate-linear in y. Ordinary gluing and evaluation are complex-linear in both skein inputs: for empty skeins in complementary balls, the displayed construction gives B(∅,i∅)=iη, whereas the declared sesquilinearity requires −iη, with η≠0. An explicit semilinear orientation-reversal/conjugation map on the second input is missing. BHMV Proposition 1.9, p.891, uses M glued to −M′ and reverses the second link; §5.8, pp.912–913, expressly distinguishes this sesquilinear pairing from the complementary bilinear pairing. Clarify the actual domains and reversal before using the coefficient-conjugate space and inverse tensor in the pairing lemma.

original_cases.reason: Ordinary complex skein gluing is bilinear, so the current definition contradicts its conjugate-linearity assertion (B(empty,i empty)=iη rather than−iη). literal_replacements.source_excerpt: Fix a marked handlebody $H$ with boundary $\Sigma$ and a complementary marked handlebody $H'$ so that their oriented gluing is the standard $S^3$; the boundary bands on $H$ and $H'$ are identified by the marking, with labels dualized on the oppositely oriented side.
literal_replacements.proposed_replacement: For connected $\Sigma$, fix marked handlebodies $H,H'$ whose boundaries are both identified orientation-preservingly with $\Sigma$, so that $H\cup_\Sigma(-H')$ is the standard oriented $S^3$. Both filling modules carry the specified boundary labels before reversal; orientation reversal of the second filling dualizes its boundary labels and reverses its ribbon-end arcs. Disconnected and empty surfaces are included by the tensor and unit convention below.

literal_replacements.source_excerpt: For $x\in\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)$ and $y\in\mathcal K_A(H';I_\Sigma,\mathbf a^*)$, glue their matching boundary bands and idempotents. This gives a closed colored ribbon graph $\Gamma$ in the standard $S^3$. Define the handlebody pairing by $B_\Sigma(x,y)=Z_p(S^3,\Gamma,w)$, using the normalized root surgery evaluation and the weight $w$ prescribed by the fixed Lagrangian data. This is the BHMV sesquilinear pairing: it is linear in $x$ and conjugate-linear in $y$ for the coefficient involution $A\mapsto A^{-1}$, $\kappa\mapsto\kappa^{-1}$.
literal_replacements.proposed_replacement: Let $\mathfrak r:\mathcal K_A(H';I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)\to\mathcal K_A(-H';-I_\Sigma,\mathbf a^*)$ be the semilinear orientation-reversal map: for a finite skein sum, $\mathfrak r(\sum_L c_L[L])=\sum_L\overline{c_L}[-L]$, with the second filling, its ribbon data and anomaly data reversed. The bar is complex conjugation, so $\overline A=A^{-1}$ and $\overline\kappa=\kappa^{-1}$. Reversal exchanges the two bracket smoothings, and conjugation exchanges their coefficients, so $\mathfrak r$ respects the skein relations and the boundary projectors. For $x\in\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)$ and $y\in\mathcal K_A(H';I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)$, glue $x$ to $\mathfrak r(y)$ along the matching boundary bands and idempotents. Denote the resulting graph by $\Gamma(x,\mathfrak r(y))$. Define $B_\Sigma(x,y)=Z_p(S^3,\Gamma(x,\mathfrak r(y)),w)$ with the prescribed gluing weight. This is linear in $x$ and conjugate-linear in $y$, as in BHMV Proposition 1.9, p.891. Ordinary gluing of two already oppositely oriented skein inputs is instead bilinear; the reversal here is part of the Definition.

original_concern.concern: The Definition permits a general closed marked surface Σ but requires complementary handlebodies whose gluing is the standard S³. This construction covers connected surfaces; it does not specify state spaces for disconnected surfaces or the empty surface, both of which occur in the stated weighted symmetric monoidal bordism category. BHMV Proposition 1.9 requires connected filling manifolds, and its complementary-handlebody example explicitly assumes connected Σ. The componentwise tensor-product construction and V_p(∅)=C need to be stated or explicitly imported before the final theorem claims a TQFT on the entire category.

original_cases.reason: A connected standard-S3 complementary-handlebody model does not itself define the whole category on disconnected/empty objects. Reference-cylinder transport retains arbitrary real Lagrangians, including nonsplit ones, rather than narrowing the object class.

Extensions agreeing outside a resolution ball can differ by an arbitrary full normal twist on a branch interval. Twisting only the positive resolution changes its self-linking by one and therefore changes the proposed finite difference. As written, the extension instruction does not uniquely determine the framed derivative; this affects the framed type definition and downstream self-linking witness.

The fixed round metric already present in the Definition supplies a canonical small transport: short-geodesic parallel transport followed by normal projection. Uniform smallness and nonvanishing near the finitely many double-point preimages keep the section nonzero; a continuous small family keeps the relative homotopy class fixed. This completes the intended framed interface without deleting framed singularities, zero resolutions, type statements or any resolved proof.

proposals.proposed_replacement: Resolve each double point by a sufficiently $C^1$-small separation of its two parameter branches, fixed outside the chosen ball. Use the fixed round metric to represent the original normal section orthogonally to the original tangent. Parallel-transport that vector along the unique short round-metric geodesic from the original branch point to its resolved point, and then project orthogonally to the normal plane of the resolved tangent. The section is nonzero near the double-point preimages, so for sufficiently small separations these projections remain nonzero and agree with the old section outside the ball. This prescribes the relative homotopy class of the transported section: no independent full normal twist may be inserted in a resolution ball. A homotopy through such small separations gives a homotopy through nonzero projected sections. Once the framing zeroes are also resolved as below, the resulting nonzero section determines a framing homotopy class.

Assume full AC for the library Jones invariant. An oriented link is a finite
disjoint union of oriented smooth circles embedded in $S^3$, considered up to
ambient isotopy; an oriented classical knot is the one-component case. For a nonempty
oriented link $L\subset S^3$, let $V_L(x)\in\mathbb Z[x^{\pm1}]$ be the
library-normalized Jones polynomial, with $V_U(x)=1$ for the unknot $U$;
write $V_K$ for its value on a knot $K$. Here $x=t^{1/2}$ in the library
convention $t=A^{-4}$, so an oriented skein triple satisfies
$$x^{-2}V_{L_+}(x)-x^2V_{L_-}(x)=(x-x^{-1})V_{L_0}(x).$$
Set $p=x-x^{-1}$. By the unique Laurent decomposition, write
$$V_K(x)=\sum_{q\ge0}(a_q(K)+b_q(K)x)p^q,$$
where $a_q(K),b_q(K)\in\mathbb Z$ and only finitely many are nonzero. The
**Jones–Vassiliev coefficient vector of order $q$** is
$$f_q(K):=(a_q(K),b_q(K))^{\mathsf T},$$
and $c_q(K):=a_q(K)+b_q(K)$. This is the algebraic coefficient-vector
definition used by Carmi and Cohen. The claim that the coordinates of $f_q$
are finite-type invariants of order at most $q$ is a separate theorem and is
not part of this definition.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}$ be the $\mathbb C$-vector space of ambient-isotopy invariants of oriented knots with values in $\mathbb C$ and type at most $n$, where type at most $n$ means that the alternating resolution sum on every $(n+1)$-singular knot is zero; set $\mathcal V_{-1}^{\mathbb C}=0$. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be the rational vector space on degree-$n$ circle chord diagrams modulo 4T and 1T; a weight system is a $\mathbb Q$-linear functional on this space. For an $n$-singular knot with chord diagram $D$, define $\sigma_n([V])(D)$ to be the $n$-fold alternating resolution sum of $V$ on that knot. Let $I_{\le n}(K)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}I_j(K)$ be the degree-$n$ truncation of the normalized unframed Kontsevich series. The degree-$n$ symbol map
$$
\sigma_n:\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}/\mathcal V_{n-1}^{\mathbb C}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}},\mathbb C)
$$
is surjective. In particular, every rational weight system has a complex-valued finite-type lift; no rationality claim is made about that lift or about the coefficients of $I(K)$. Moreover, for every $n$ and every $V\in\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}$ there is a complex-linear functional $\Lambda_V$ on $\bigoplus_{j=0}^{n}(\mathcal A_j^{\mathrm{un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$ whose degree-$n$ restriction is the degree-$n$ symbol of $V$ and such that
$$
V(K)=\Lambda_V(I_{\le n}(K))
$$
for every oriented knot type $K$. This recovery statement does not imply that distinct knot types have distinct Kontsevich series.

Assume full AC for the library Jones invariant. An oriented link is a finite
disjoint union of oriented smooth circles embedded in $S^3$, considered up to
ambient isotopy; an oriented classical knot is the one-component case. For a nonempty
oriented link $L\subset S^3$, let $V_L(x)\in\mathbb Z[x^{\pm1}]$ be the
library-normalized Jones polynomial, with $V_U(x)=1$ for the unknot $U$;
write $V_K$ for its value on a knot $K$. Here $x=t^{1/2}$ in the library
convention $t=A^{-4}$, so an oriented skein triple satisfies
$$x^{-2}V_{L_+}(x)-x^2V_{L_-}(x)=(x-x^{-1})V_{L_0}(x).$$
Set $p=x-x^{-1}$. By the unique Laurent decomposition, write
$$V_K(x)=\sum_{q\ge0}(a_q(K)+b_q(K)x)p^q,$$
where $a_q(K),b_q(K)\in\mathbb Z$ and only finitely many are nonzero. The
**Jones–Vassiliev coefficient vector of order $q$** is
$$f_q(K):=(a_q(K),b_q(K))^{\mathsf T},$$
and $c_q(K):=a_q(K)+b_q(K)$. This is the algebraic coefficient-vector
definition used by Carmi and Cohen. The claim that the coordinates of $f_q$
are finite-type invariants of order at most $q$ is a separate theorem and is
not part of this definition.

consumers.public_clause_literal: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. replacements.proposed_replacement: Apply [F6]'s planar supplier successively with exactly two inner faces, rather than once to this whole cap. Choose a finite tree of disjoint joining bands in the cap, rooted at its unique $D_i$ face, and process it outward from the root. At each stage the frontier of a small neighborhood of the processed subtree is the moving rim. A thin neighborhood of that moving face, the next unused face and their joining band is a disk with two holes whose interior misses every other current face and z. Its two labels are the current moving disk and a retained $D_j$ with $j\ne i$, so the supplier's distinct-disk hypothesis holds with $r=1$. Its completed slide preserves the cut ball and the retained disks. Use its finger-retraction identification, supported at that face and band, to carry the unprocessed cap and its remaining faces to the new cut-ball boundary; outside that neighborhood the unused faces are unchanged. Thus the next stage has the same description. If both faces of a retained disk occur, the second remains an unused face of that retained disk and is processed by a later two-face application; it is never paired with its other face in one application. A tiny auxiliary trivial arc near z, with second endpoint w, can be fixed before this construction and missed by all these cap neighborhoods, so the supplier's marked arc condition is retained. After finitely many stages the moving rim is the frontier of the whole tree neighborhood, and the remaining empty annulus in the cap gives the isotopy to $\partial D_i'$.

replacements.proposed_replacement: 2.1 Regard $T$ and $T_0$ as finite linear complexes on the same embedded polyhedron $Q$. Form all nonempty cells $\sigma\cap\tau$ for $\sigma\in T$ and $\tau\in T_0$, together with their faces. More decisively, the defined object is the equivalence relation generated by slides, so inverse framed band slides are already admitted: reversing the same band in its product neighborhood subtracts the stationary framed parallel and retains its full framing. Thus signed slides do not change the generated relation. The actual zero-meridian proof uses finite move equivalence and transports the stationary component orientation; its negative signed slides are inverse positive slides if the narrower orientation convention is adopted. An explicit auxiliary-orientation sentence would improve readability, but this concern does not establish a false equivalence or missing mathematical permission.

patches.kind: Statement: specify actual cut track and distinguish handle model from covering map
patches.source_excerpt: Push the interior of $F$ into $B^4$ while keeping $K$ on $S^3=\partial B^4$, cut $B^4$ along a thickened copy of the pushed-in surface, and take $q$ copies. For $i=1,\ldots,q-1$, glue the positive face of copy $i$ to the negative face of copy $i+1$ by reflecting the normal coordinate; do not glue the last positive face to the first negative face. Call the resulting $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $W_q(F)$. It has one $0$-handle and $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles, and its framed attaching link has linking matrix $M_q(V)$. The boundary branched cover, with the boundary marking induced by the covering map, is $\Sigma_q(K)$.
patches.proposed_replacement: Push the interior of $F$ into $B^4$ while keeping $K$ on $S^3=\partial B^4$, and let $W_q(F)$ be the actual $q$-fold cyclic branched cover along that pushed-in surface. Use the following disk-band handle model of this cover. Cut $B^4$ along the three-dimensional track of the push-in isotopy; the cut-open manifold is again a $4$-ball and its boundary contains the thickened surface $\bar F=(F\times[-1,1])/\sim$, where $(x,t)\sim(x,t')$ for $x\in\partial F$. Write $\bar F^\pm=\{(x,t)\in\bar F:\pm t\ge0\}$. Take $q$ copies of this cut-open ball and, for $i=1,\ldots,q-1$, glue $\bar F_i^+$ to $\bar F_{i+1}^-$ by $(x,t)\mapsto(x,-t)$. The Akbulut–Kirby construction identifies this handle model with $W_q(F)$; the last-to-first gluing is unnecessary for the underlying manifold in this model. This is a statement about the isotopy-track handle model, not an assertion that an open chain of normal-disk sectors is already the cyclic covering map. The resulting handle presentation has one $0$-handle and $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles, and its framed attaching link has linking matrix $M_q(V)$. The boundary branched cover, with the boundary marking induced by the covering map of $W_q(F)$, is $\Sigma_q(K)$.

patches.proposed_replacement:
[F4] The $q$-fold branched cover of $S^3$ is formed from the meridian-mod-$q$ cover of the compact exterior by filling the lift of $\mu^q$. [[def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot]]

[F5] **External input (Akbulut–Kirby disk-band construction).** For a connected oriented Seifert surface in $S^3$, pushed into $B^4$, the $q$-fold cyclic branched cover is represented by cutting along the push-in isotopy track and gluing $q$ cut-open balls along the thickened half-surfaces as specified above, using only the $q-1$ adjacent-copy gluings. The terminal gluing is unnecessary for the underlying manifold. If the surface has one disk and $b$ bands, the disk gluings give one $0$-handle; each band gives one $2$-handle at each of the $q-1$ layers, with attaching circle obtained from the two corresponding face-core arcs and with the carried band framing. The actual branched covering map restricts on the boundary to the cyclic cover branched along the boundary link. This is the explicitly imported construction of Akbulut–Kirby, §2, printed pp.113–114 and the boundary-restriction Remark p.116; the paper's smooth oriented conventions are on p.111. It is not claimed as a locally reconstructed handle-identification proof. [Akbulut–Kirby, *Branched Covers of Surfaces in 4-Manifolds*, Math. Ann.252 (1980),111–131](https://math.berkeley.edu/~kirby/papers/Akbulut%20and%20Kirby%20-%20Branched%20covers%20of%20surfaces%20in%204-manifolds%20-%20MR0593626.pdf).

patches.kind: Proof1.1 source-qualified handle identification; counts retained
patches.source_excerpt: 1.1 By [F1] and [F2], cut $B^4$ along the thickening of the pushed-in disk-band surface, producing cut copies $B_1^4,\ldots,B_q^4$. First glue these copies only along the disk $0$-handle of the branch surface. A disk thickening is a $3$-ball in the boundary of each cut $4$-ball; joining the two face balls for consecutive copies is the standard boundary-connected-sum operation, so the resulting $4$-manifold is again a $4$-ball with one $0$-handle. For each surface band, the positive face of copy $k$ glued to the negative face of copy $k+1$ joins the two band-core arcs; its regular neighborhood is a $2$-handle $D^2\times D^2$ attached along $S^1\times D^2$. There are $q-1$ such seams and $2g$ bands, so the construction gives $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles and no other handles. [A1, F1, F2, given, construct]
patches.proposed_replacement: 1.1 Use the isotopy-track handle model supplied by [F5], not a cut of the codimension-two branch surface itself. By [F1] and [F2], the connected surface has one disk and $2g$ bands. In the model, the disk-face gluings combine the $q$ cut-open $4$-balls into a $4$-ball with one $0$-handle. The remaining face gluings give, for each band and each adjacent-copy layer $k=1,\ldots,q-1$, a $2$-handle whose attaching circle joins that band's two face-core arcs through the common disk region, with the carried band framing. Hence there are $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles and no other handles. The identification of this model with the actual cyclic branched cover, including the legitimacy of omitting the terminal gluing, is the external input [F5]; the local linking-entry computation below uses its attaching-circle description. [A1, F1, F2, F5, given, construct]

patches.kind: Proof3.1 actual covering map and marked boundary
patches.source_excerpt: 3.1 In a normal disk to the branch surface, the $q$ cut sheets form the standard cyclic degree-$q$ branched disk; its map is $w\mapsto w^q$. Away from the branch locus, a positive meridian moves through the $q$ sheets cyclically, so the boundary exterior cover is the connected cover classified by the homomorphism $\pi_1(E_K)\to\mathbb Z/q$ sending $\mu$ to $1$. Its meridian boundary is the closed lift of $\mu^q$, which bounds the filling disk. By [F4] and uniqueness of the classified connected cover, the boundary with its branch marking is $\Sigma_q(K)$. The innermost-disk construction makes its interior disjoint from the curves. proposed_operations.source_excerpt: 2.1 Suppose $\gamma_0,\gamma_1$ are essential simple closed curves whose primitive classes agree up to sign. Reverse one orientation if necessary so their classes agree, and isotope them to be transverse. Let $v$ be their common primitive class and let $A=\mathbb R^2/\langle T_v\rangle$ be the cyclic cover of $T$ corresponding to the subgroup generated by $v$. A lift of each curve to $A$ is an embedded essential circle representing the generator of $H_1(A;\mathbb Z)$. Their algebraic intersection in the annulus $A$ is zero, so if they meet the signed crossing count in a fundamental period has both signs. Lift these circles to the universal cover $\mathbb R^2$ of $A$. Their chosen lifts are proper lines invariant under the same translation $T_v$; they have the same two ends at infinity. Opposite-sign crossings on this pair of lines have a bounded complementary disk between subarcs, by the Jordan curve theorem. Among all such disks choose one with the fewest interior intersections with lifted curves, and among ties one of least transverse width modulo the deck translations. Any lifted arc entering its interior cuts off a disk with fewer interior intersections; any nontrivial translate meeting it yields a disk of smaller transverse width. Thus its interior misses every lift and translate, so it projects injectively to an embedded bigon in $T$. Isotoping one curve across this bigon removes exactly two intersections and creates none. Since the original intersection set is finite, repetition terminates and makes the curves disjoint. Cutting $T$ along $\gamma_0$ gives an annulus, and the disjoint essential curve $\gamma_1$ is parallel to its core, so the two curves cobound a subannulus. Isotopy across that annulus carries $\gamma_0$ to $\gamma_1$. Thus the primitive class modulo simultaneous sign determines exactly one unoriented isotopy class. [given, A1, step 1.1, step 1.2, construct] ∎
proposed_operations.proposed_replacement: 2.1 Suppose $\gamma_0,\gamma_1$ are essential simple closed curves whose primitive classes agree up to sign. Reverse one orientation if necessary so their classes agree, and isotope them to be transverse. Let $v\in\mathbb Z^2$ be their common primitive class in the coordinates of [A1]. If they intersect, choose lifts $\widetilde\gamma_0,\widetilde\gamma_1\subset\mathbb R^2$ through one lift $x$ of an intersection point. Each chosen lift is preserved by the same nonzero deck translation $T_v$, because its projected curve represents $v$. Hence both $x$ and $T_v(x)$ lie on this pair of lifts and are distinct. By [F1] the curves therefore form an embedded bigon in $T$ whose interior misses them. Isotoping one curve across this bigon removes exactly two intersections and creates none. The transverse intersection set is finite, so repetition terminates and makes the curves disjoint. Cutting $T$ along $\gamma_0$ gives an annulus, and the disjoint essential curve $\gamma_1$ is parallel to its core, so the two curves cobound a subannulus. Isotopy across that annulus carries $\gamma_0$ to $\gamma_1$. Thus the primitive class modulo simultaneous sign determines exactly one unoriented isotopy class. The uniform needle bound lacks a uniform separation hypothesis. Step 1.2 says, “compactness and embeddedness give a uniform positive lower bound for |z-z′|,” but embeddedness for each ε and compact control of the critical-point charts do not prevent another regular strand from approaching the needle as ε→0. Locally take the fixed Morse cap z=s, t=−s², |s|≤ε/2, and another upward strand z=iε. The cap has horizontal diameter ε and its critical chart is unchanged. Its two signed degree-one mixed-chord integrals sum, up to orientation sign, to (2πi)⁻¹ log((1/2−i)/(−1/2−i)), a nonzero constant; the chord joins different skeleton components and survives tangle 1T. These local pieces can be extended by regular arcs inside a fixed slab. Thus the written chart assumptions do not justify Cmε uniformly. The cited CDM §8.6.2 argument also uses opposite-branch cancellation rather than the claimed individual absolute long-chord estimate. The convergence assertion for a fixed tangle is a separate issue.

The Definition starts with an arbitrary balanced sutured manifold and says: 'Two such fields are homologous when, outside some open ball in int M, they are homotopic'. Balanced manifolds here may be disconnected. On two disjoint product balls, take fields v, w, z with the fixed boundary values: w differs from v by one local Hopf modification in the first component, and z differs from w by one in the second. Then v is related to w and w to z, but v is not related to z: a single ball lies in one component, leaving a nontrivial relative Hopf difference in the other. Thus the stated relation is not transitive and does not define homology classes at this scope. The empty balanced manifold also has no ball witnessing reflexivity. The original [Juhász 2006, §4](https://msp.org/agt/2006/6-3/agt-v6-n3-p16-s.pdf) explicitly assumes connectedness before this definition. The actual knot exteriors are connected, but the general definition needs adjudication.

required_operations.source_excerpt: 2.1 By [F3] and [F4], the index-two kernel determines a connected two-sheeted cover. On the boundary of a punctured tube around $K_i$, its two monodromies are the prescribed meridian value $1$ and a longitude value $\eta_i\in\mathbb F_2$. The local model [F5] has exactly those two monodromies; classification of covers of the punctured tube identifies it with the restricted cover. The displayed model therefore extends the cover across every branch component. If a tubular framing is changed by $k$ meridional twists, the parallel longitude changes by $k\mu_i$, so its character changes by $k$ modulo two; the corresponding rotation of the normal coordinate changes the phase in the local model by the same parity. Thus these are coordinate descriptions of one extension, not different covers. [F3, F4, F5, step 1.1]
required_operations.proposed_replacement:
2.1 By [F3] and [F4], the index-two kernel determines a connected two-sheeted cover. On a punctured tube around $K_i$, its two monodromies are the meridian value $1$ and a longitude value $\eta_i\in\mathbb F_2$. The local model [F5] has exactly these monodromies, so covering classification identifies its punctured part with the restricted cover. Attach its core to obtain a smooth extension in the chosen charts. This constructs an extension; independence of the smooth total-space diffeomorphism type requires the normalization below, not merely equality of boundary monodromies. [F3, F4, F5, step 1.1]

2.2 Compare two oriented tubular charts $\varphi_0,\varphi_1$ around the same component. Express them over a common oriented core parameter $s$; a change of the original core parameter only replaces the unit phase $e^{\mathrm i\eta_j s}$ by a smooth unit loop $a_j(s)$ of the same winding number $\eta_j$. Let $A(s)\in GL^+(2,\mathbb R)$ be the unique vertical linear change for which $\varphi_1\circ A$ and $\varphi_0$ induce the same normal-quotient identification. Write $A=RP$ by smooth polar decomposition, with $R(s)\in SO(2)$ and $P(s)$ positive definite. The compatible-tube assertion [F6] gives an ambient isotopy fixing the core and carrying $\varphi_0$ to $\varphi_1\circ A$ near it. The fiber-linear isotopy $R((1-t)P+tI)$ then connects $A$ to $R$ through invertible maps. On a common smaller tube its composition with $\varphi_1$ is an isotopy of open embeddings, with open track, fixing the core. The relative open-set clause of [F6] extends it near the compact core. Thus an ambient diffeomorphism $g$, isotopic to the identity through maps fixing the whole link, satisfies $g\circ\varphi_0=\varphi_1\circ R$ near this component. Choose the supports in disjoint component tubes and compose the finitely many isotopies. [F6, given, construct]

2.3 Identify $R(s)$ with a unit complex number, of winding $k$. The two signs of $r$ differ by the deck map. Choose the sign matching the complement-cover isomorphism at one point of each connected punctured tube; covering uniqueness makes them agree throughout that tube. Hence the local lifts glue to the complement lift. This proves independence of the oriented smooth total-space diffeomorphism type from arbitrary oriented tubular charts. required_operations.source_excerpt: Fix a finite regular diagram $D$ of a nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, choose a basepoint $p\in D$ away from the crossings, and choose an admissible pointed Heegaard multi-diagram subordinate to the branched-cover surgeries, with the compatible perturbation data and top-generator cycles of the link-surgery construction. Identify each first-page vertex group with the reduced state space of the corresponding crossingless resolution, based at the circle containing $p$. For every cube edge, the induced first differential is the mod-two map assigned by the saddle: multiplication when two resolution circles merge and comultiplication when one resolution circle splits, with the marked-circle quotient at $p$. Under these identifications the direct sum of edge maps is the reduced Khovanov differential of the mirror diagram $\overline D$, based at the corresponding point, in the Ozsváth–Szabó smoothing convention.

required_operations.source_excerpt: For every integer $k\ge1$, let $U_k\subset S^3$ be a $k$-component planar unlink with an arbitrary orientation on each component, and choose a basepoint $p$ on any one component. Its double branched cover is $\#^{\,k-1}(S^2\times S^1)$, with $\Sigma(U_1)=S^3$. Over $\mathbb F_2$, the hat Floer group of this cover is identified with the exterior algebra on a $(k-1)$-dimensional vector space, hence has rank $2^{k-1}$. Under these identifications, the cobordism maps for saddle cobordisms between neighboring unlink resolutions, with $p$ carried outside the saddle disk, are the multiplication and comultiplication maps of the two-dimensional Frobenius algebra $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$ after reduction at the marked component. The identification includes the marked-circle cases and fixes the basis conventions needed to compare the first surgery differential with the reduced Khovanov cube.

required_operations.source_excerpt: Its abelianization under $x\mapsto q$, $y\mapsto p$ is $cq-dp=-1$, so it is opposite the positive normal-disk meridian, whose class is the positive generator by [F3].
required_operations.proposed_replacement: To calibrate signs geometrically, the positively oriented coordinate cores representing $x$ and $y$ bound the hemispherical disks $D_x=\{\operatorname{Im}z_2=0,\ \operatorname{Re}z_2\ge0\}\cap S^3$ and $D_y=\{\operatorname{Im}z_1=0,\ \operatorname{Re}z_1\ge0\}\cap S^3$, oriented by their respective core boundaries. The knot meets $D_x$ transversely in $|q|$ points, each with intersection sign $\operatorname{sgn}(q)$, and meets $D_y$ in $|p|$ points, each with sign $\operatorname{sgn}(p)$. For the first sign, at a point where $z_2$ is positive real, the ambient orientation is the complex $z_1$ orientation followed by increasing $\operatorname{Im}z_2$; the component of the knot tangent transverse to $D_x$ has sign $q$. For the second, at positive real $z_1$, the ambient orientation is increasing $\operatorname{Im}z_1$ followed by the complex $z_2$ orientation, and the transverse tangent component has sign $p$. Deleting small disks about these intersections gives oriented surfaces in the knot complement with boundary relations $[x]=q[\mu]$ and $[y]=p[\mu]$, where $\mu$ is the positive normal-disk meridian. Thus the abelianization $x\mapsto q$, $y\mapsto p$ sends this geometric meridian to $1$: [F3] makes $[\mu]$ a generator, and the displayed relations and $\gcd(p,q)=1$ fix its sign. The disk-boundary curve $m$ has abelianization $cq-dp=-1$, so its orientation is opposite to that positive meridian.

concern.concern: Definition Step 4 says to retain segment labels and their designated endpoints through smoothings, then start each closed component at its least-labelled segment. Smoothing can cut one labelled polygonal segment into multiple surviving pieces, potentially on different components; its original designated endpoints need not remain endpoints of those pieces. No subdivision/relabeling or tie-breaking rule is specified. The claimed deterministic traversal needs this bookkeeping clause; the procedure-properties proof 1.2 assumes it is already determined.

required_operations.source_excerpt:
$g_i^{\pm1}T_\mu$. In each current diagram, orient open strands from the smaller to the larger endpoint
   label and order them by their initial endpoints. Order closed components by
   their least segment labels. In each closed component, start by traversing its
   least-labelled segment from its designated initial endpoint to its terminal
   endpoint; then follow the unique continuation of that component, traversing
   later segments in whichever direction reaches the next endpoint. At a crossing
   continue along the same strand, and after a smoothing continue along the
   prescribed pairing. Retain segment labels and their designated endpoints
   through switches and smoothings. This gives a deterministic traversal even
   when segment orientations do not join coherently around a closed component.
required_operations.proposed_replacement:
$g_i^{\pm1}T_\mu$. For each initial reducer input (a matrix column here or a
   closed trace diagram in Step 5), first fix pairwise disjoint rational crossing
   boxes, each meeting only its two crossing branches, in four boundary ports,
   and containing no polygonal vertex. Choose the first admissible finite tuple
   in the length-then-lexicographic rational coding order of Step 3. Make the
   boxes small enough that every component contains a segment portion outside
   the boxes. Subdivide all polygonal segments at their box-boundary ports.
   Give the portions outside the boxes fresh distinct labels in their finite
   diagram-code order; designate the lexicographically smaller coordinate
   endpoint of each portion as its initial endpoint. Retain these portions,
   labels, and endpoints throughout that reduction tree. Inside each box record
   either the original crossing pairing or one of its two smoothing pairings;
   switches change only over/under data, and smoothings change only this pairing.
   In each current diagram, orient open strands from the smaller to the larger
   boundary endpoint label and order them by their initial endpoints. Order
   closed components by their least portion labels. Start each closed component
   along its least-labelled portion from its designated initial endpoint to its
   other endpoint, then follow its unique continuation. Inside a crossing box
   follow its current pairing. No portion is split or relabelled by a switch or
   smoothing, and every resulting component contains a labelled portion. This
   determines the traversal even when the designated directions of successive
   portions disagree.

required_operations.source_excerpt: **Finite comparison rules:** Two normalized codes represent the same code class when some bijection of their finite crossing labels and edge labels carries all dart incidences, crossing rotations, orientations, signs, component cycles, and outer-face data of one code to the other. To test whether two codes differ by one move, enumerate all finite choices of local edge intervals and crossing subrecords of sizes allowed by R1, R2, or R3; test that the codes agree outside the chosen disk boundary and that the two local records are one of the standard orientation/sign variants of that move. The local-site test uses the exact variants in the oriented Reidemeister-move definition.
required_operations.proposed_replacement:
**Finite comparison rules:** Two normalized codes represent the same code class when some bijection of their finite crossing labels and edge labels carries all dart incidences, crossing rotations, orientations, signs, component cycles, and outer-face data of one code to the other. For a move-site test use the finite spherical cellulation returned by reconstruction and mark a point at infinity in its distinguished outer face. For the crossingless circle, insert one auxiliary degree-two vertex and use its two complementary face disks; this vertex is suppressed in all comparisons.

For each of $m=2,4,6$, enumerate every distribution of $m$ distinct cut points among diagram edges and every linear order of the points on each edge. Use one representative of each order (for example equally spaced interior points); their numerical positions are immaterial. In each face disk enumerate noncrossing pairings of all boundary occurrences of these cut points by interior arcs. In the distinguished face also record which complementary region contains the marked point at infinity. Glue the face arcs at the cut points and retain only choices forming a single simple closed curve. Cutting the finite cellulation along these arcs and flooding across incident cell pieces identifies the two sides; select the side not containing infinity. This is the candidate closed move disk. Its entire diagram intersection, including every vertex, edge segment and possible closed component inside it, must be isomorphic relative to its cyclically ordered boundary points to one side of a standard R1, R2 or R3 template with the chosen orientation/sign variant. In particular no additional diagram portion is permitted inside the disk. All tests are finite incidence and cyclic-order comparisons. The same construction is performed for the other code, requiring the opposite side of the same template and an isomorphism of the outside records fixing the ordered boundary points, all decorations and the infinity region. Store the cut orders, face pairings, selected regions, template variant and outside isomorphism as the certificate.

There are finitely many cut distributions, orders, face pairings and region choices. Every move disk has two, four or six transverse boundary intersections, avoids crossing vertices, and cuts each face into disjoint arcs; it therefore has a representative among these choices. Moving cut points along an edge and face arcs within a face disk changes neither the inside tangle nor the outside code class. Thus the test includes every admissible move disk, including move creation from the crossingless circle, and accepts only genuine disk-supported template replacements. The local templates and their exact orientation/sign variants are those in the oriented Reidemeister-move definition.

concern.concern: The uniform needle bound lacks a uniform separation hypothesis. Step 1.2 says, “compactness and embeddedness give a uniform positive lower bound for |z-z′|,” but embeddedness for each ε and compact control of the critical-point charts do not prevent another regular strand from approaching the needle as ε→0. Locally take the fixed Morse cap z=s, t=−s², |s|≤ε/2, and another upward strand z=iε. The cap has horizontal diameter ε and its critical chart is unchanged. Its two signed degree-one mixed-chord integrals sum, up to orientation sign, to (2πi)⁻¹ log((1/2−i)/(−1/2−i)), a nonzero constant; the chord joins different skeleton components and survives tangle 1T. These local pieces can be extended by regular arcs inside a fixed slab. Thus the written chart assumptions do not justify Cmε uniformly. The cited CDM §8.6.2 argument also uses opposite-branch cancellation rather than the claimed individual absolute long-chord estimate. The convergence assertion for a fixed tangle is a separate issue.

required_operations.proposed_replacement: For the following uniform local-cap estimate, assume additionally a fixed finite system of disjoint critical bands and intervening regular bands, with uniformly bounded branch derivatives in their height or Morse coordinates. Assume the critical charts vary in a compact smooth family and their linear terms are uniformly bounded away from zero, and that every equal-height pair other than the two branches meeting at the same critical point has horizontal separation at least a fixed $d>0$, independent of $\varepsilon$. Require $N_\varepsilon$ to lie in one of these Morse charts with parameter range $0\le s\le A\varepsilon$, for a fixed $A$. Then, for every fixed $m$, the sum of degree-$m$ pairing integrals with at least one endpoint on $N_\varepsilon$ has norm at most $C_m\varepsilon$, with $C_m$ independent of $\varepsilon$. Thus these contributions tend to zero under these uniformity hypotheses. No such uniform estimate is asserted for an unrelated strand approaching the needle as $\varepsilon\to0$; convergence for each fixed knot or tangle is unaffected.

required_operations.source_excerpt: 1.2 For a long chord with one endpoint on the needle and one outside it, compactness and embeddedness give a uniform positive lower bound for $|z-z'|$ on each compact branch chart. In the Morse parameter $s$, both endpoint evaluations are smooth, so the one-form $d\log(z-z')$ has norm at most $C\,ds$. The range of $s$ along a width-$\varepsilon$ needle is at most $C\varepsilon$, since $|z_+(s)-z_-(s)|\asymp s$. Thus integrating such a chord endpoint over any subinterval of the needle costs at most $C\varepsilon$. This is a direct absolute estimate for each pairing term and does not identify diagrams obtained from opposite branch choices. The constants are uniform in the stated compact smooth family. [given, F1, F2, construct, algebra]
required_operations.proposed_replacement: 1.2 For a fixed knot or tangle, a long chord in a sufficiently small critical chart has nonzero limiting separation at the critical point, so its denominator is bounded below by some positive constant. In the uniform local-cap family, the additional separation hypothesis supplies the same lower bound $d$ independently of $\varepsilon$. The branch derivative bounds in the Morse parameter give $|d(z-z')|\le C\,ds$, hence $|d\log(z-z')|\le (C/d)\,ds$ uniformly. The stipulated range $0\le s\le A\varepsilon$ then bounds the integral of this factor by $CA\varepsilon/d$; on a subinterval $(0,\delta)$ it is at most $C\delta/d$. These are individual absolute estimates under the stated uniformity hypotheses. They do not replace the opposite-branch cancellation used for more general special critical movements in the cited sources. [given, F1, F2, construct, algebra]

concern.concern: The Definition starts with an arbitrary balanced sutured manifold and says: 'Two such fields are homologous when, outside some open ball in int M, they are homotopic'. Balanced manifolds here may be disconnected. On two disjoint product balls, take fields v, w, z with the fixed boundary values: w differs from v by one local Hopf modification in the first component, and z differs from w by one in the second. Then v is related to w and w to z, but v is not related to z: a single ball lies in one component, leaving a nontrivial relative Hopf difference in the other. Thus the stated relation is not transitive and does not define homology classes at this scope. The empty balanced manifold also has no ball witnessing reflexivity. The original [Juhász 2006, §4](https://msp.org/agt/2006/6-3/agt-v6-n3-p16-s.pdf) explicitly assumes connectedness before this definition. The actual knot exteriors are connected, but the general definition needs adjudication.

required_operations.source_excerpt: 1.2 Suppose that $\lambda$ is a translation-invariant Borel measure finite on every bounded Borel set. Put $U_j=\{x:\|x-e_j\|_2<1/3\}$. For $j\ne k$, $\|e_j-e_k\|_2=\sqrt2>2/3$, so the $U_j$ are pairwise disjoint. Each lies in the bounded ball $\{x:\|x\|_2<2\}$ by the triangle inequality. Translation invariance gives $\lambda(U_j)=m$ independent of $j$. If $m>0$, the first $N$ disjoint balls have total measure $Nm$ for every $N$, contradicting finiteness of the radius-two ball. Hence $m=0$. [F2, given, algebra]
required_operations.proposed_replacement: 1.2 Suppose that $\lambda$ is a nonzero locally finite translation-invariant Borel measure, where locally finite means that every point has a neighborhood of finite measure. At zero choose $R>0$ with $\lambda(B(0,R))<\infty$. Put $r=R/8$ and $U_j=B((R/2)e_j,r)$. For $j\ne k$ the distance between the centers is $R/\sqrt2>2r$, so these balls are pairwise disjoint, and every $U_j$ lies in $B(0,R)$ because $R/2+r<R$. Translation invariance gives a common finite mass $m=\lambda(U_j)$. If $m>0$, finite additivity and monotonicity give $Nm\le\lambda(B(0,R))$ for every $N$, a contradiction. Hence $m=0$. We use the scalar calculation of [[lem-standard-normal-fourth-moment]] with this supplied law, rather than invoke its AC-based law construction: $\varphi\prime(t)=-t\varphi(t)$, so integration by parts on $[-R,R]$ gives $\int t^2\varphi=[-t\varphi]_{-R}^R+\int\varphi$ and $\int t^4\varphi=[-t^3\varphi]_{-R}^R+3\int t^2\varphi$. The polynomial-Gaussian boundary terms vanish as $R\to\infty$; the nonnegative integrals increase to their full integrals. Supplied normalization therefore gives second and fourth moments $1$ and $3$; symmetry gives first and third moments zero. This supplied-law calculation uses no additional choice.

concern.concern: The Statement defines a positive Hopf band solely as 'an oriented annulus whose two boundary components, with their induced orientations, have linking number +1.' This omits the unknotted-core condition. A framed annulus around a nontrivial knot can satisfy this linking condition. Knotting the b-annulus away from the plumbing square and the specified disk for a⁺ preserves the stated linking/intersection conditions and matrix calculation, but does not justify the trefoil boundary identification in Proof 1.1. The later word 'standard' needs an explicit restriction consistent with the initial definition. The conventional missing condition is explicit in Quach Hongler–Weber, §2, printed p. 137: [The link of an extrovert divide](https://www.numdam.org/article/AFST_2000_6_9_1_133_0.pdf). Thus the definition and trefoil identification appear overbroad as written, although the displayed matrix follows from the other specified conditions.

concern.concern: Proof 5.1 concludes that each field evaluation is measurable with respect to the completion of G=σ(Y(e_n):n), and hence that the full field sigma-algebra is contained in that completion. Almost-sure equality with a G-measurable variable only gives this for the ambient augmentation by all ambient null events; it need not give membership in the ordinary completion of G. For example, take X=H=R, K=0, ε=1, an independent standard-normal prior U, standard-normal ξ and an independent Bernoulli(0) coordinate with event N={coordinate=1}. Set Z(g)=gξ except Z(2)=2ξ+1_N. This satisfies the stated Gaussian and L2-linearity assumptions. With supplied basis {1}, G=σ(ξ), while the full field reveals N through Y(2)−2Y(1). N is not contained in any G-measurable null set. The theorem's independence conclusion remains accessible directly from the already established independence with every finite observation block and a generating-cylinder argument, but the written completion inclusion needs qualification.
